extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic/anabelian geometry (readers of Mochizuki/IUT-style work)
extracted.subtask_description: Group-theoretic reconstruction (mono-anabelian) results and required hypotheses for recovering geometric objects (orbicurves, decomposition groups, coverings, function field additive structure) from profinite/arithmetic fundamental groups. Focuses on cuspidalisation (elliptic and Belyi), rigidity of inertia, Uchida-style reconstruction, and necessary field/group hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slimness (property 'slim')
rubrics_metrics.description: (slim) holds in the case where k is an NF by Proposition 2.7 (1)(d) or k is an MLF by Proposition 2.7 (1)(c). More generally, it holds for Kummer-faithful field k by Remark 3.17.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slimness of the target profinite group G is used repeatedly (e.g., Lemma 3.5) to obtain uniqueness statements for homomorphisms and to make pro-finite-group theory parallel geometry (Remark 3.5.1). In practice assume k sub-p-adic, NF, MLF, or Kummer-faithful to guarantee slimness of G (and hence various epimorphism/uniqueness consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cuspidal characterisation ((Cusp)X)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Cusp)X holds for any X in the case where k is an MLF by Corollary 2.9. More generally, (Cusp)X holds for l-cyclotomically full field k for some l under the assumption (Delta)'X (Remark 2.9.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Cusp)X is the group-theoretic characterisation of cuspidal inertia/decomposition subgroups; when it holds the cuspidal inertia subgroups are group-theoretically identifiable and can be used to form cuspidal quotients and to reconstruct decomposition groups (used in Lemma 3.6 and Theorems 3.7/3.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global compatibility condition (Delta)X / (Delta)'X
rubrics_metrics.description: (Delta)X (and the weakened form (Delta)'X) is assumed in many reconstructions; for NF or MLF fields (Delta)X holds for any X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Delta)X provides the surjection π1(X) → G_k which is used as input datum for reconstruction; when (Delta)X (or (Delta)'X) is available one may avoid including certain subgroups as additional input. Many reconstruction theorems (elliptic/Belyi cuspidalisation) assume (Delta)'X implicitly via this quotient data.

rubrics_metrics.name: (GC) (geometric compatibility) hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: (GC) is asserted to hold in the table for certain base-field hypotheses (e.g., sub-p-adic cases) and is used to identify geometric objects from group data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (GC) allows passage from group actions to actions on geometric coverings (used in proofs of Lemma 3.6(2), Theorem 3.7, etc.). When (GC) holds, functors from geometric coverings to the LocG((π1)) category are equivalences, enabling group-theoretic reconstruction of the corresponding coverings and quotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention for 'group-theoretic algorithm' / mono- vs bi-anabelian phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: It seems difficult to rigorously formulate 'there is a group-theoretic algorithm to reconstruct' something in the sense of mono-anabelian approach; to be rigorous the algorithm itself should be part of the statement. The survey uses the phrase 'group-theoretic algorithm' loosely, making input and output data of the algorithms in the statement clear (Remark 3.4.4 (2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one wishes full rigor when claiming existence of a group-theoretic reconstruction algorithm, the algorithm must be stated explicitly. In practice the proofs provide concrete constructions, so the survey states results informally with the understanding that the constructions in the proofs supply the rigorous algorithm. Mono-anabelian approach yields 'model-free' reconstruction of objects themselves (not only isomorphisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of open homomorphisms under slimness (Lemma 3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let ϕ: H → Π be open and α1, α2: Π → G open homomorphisms; assume G is slim. If α1 ◦ ϕ = α2 ◦ ϕ then α1 = α2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used repeatedly to deduce uniqueness of certain quotient/surjection structures determined by compatibility conditions. Practically: when constructing group-theoretic quotients or lifts, impose slimness of the target G to ensure uniqueness (no nontrivial central ambiguity arises).

rubrics_metrics.name: Epimorphism property for inclusions when target is slim (Remark 3.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: In algebraic geometry a finite étale covering Y → X is an epimorphism; if π1(X) is slim then the inclusion map π1(Y) → π1(X) corresponding to Y→X is also an epimorphism in the profinite group category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows one to treat pro-finite-group constructions analogously to geometric coverings without invoking higher-categorical machinery, provided involved pro-finite groups are slim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction operations for cuspidalisations (Lemma 3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three operations used in elliptic and Belyi cuspidalisations: (1) an open immersion π1'' → π1' arises from a finite étale covering and reconstructs π1 of the cover; (2) an open immersion π1' → π1'' with a compatible surjection to an open subgroup of G uniquely determines that surjection and arises from a finite étale quotient; (3) a surjection π1' → π1'' whose kernel is generated by a cuspidal inertia subgroup (group-theoretically characterised) arises from an open immersion of schemes (a cuspidal quotient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performing cuspidalisations group-theoretically, verify that the relevant immersion/surjection fits one of these three patterns; (GC) and (Cusp)X inputs are used to translate between group-theoretic data and geometric coverings/quotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elliptic cuspidalisation reconstructability (Theorem 3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be an elliptically admissible orbicurve over a sub-p-adic field k. For positive integer N and the open sub-orbicurve UX;N determined by torsion points, from the profinite groups (π1)X and its geometric kernel one can group-theoretically reconstruct the surjection π1(UX;N) → π1(X) induced by the open immersion UX;N ↪ X and the set of decomposition groups at points of X \, UX;N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input required: arithmetic fundamental group π1(X) and its geometric kernel (π1^geom). Assumptions: X elliptically admissible, k sub-p-adic (so G_k slim). The proof proceeds by forming Loc_G((π1)) categories, reconstructing core groups, identifying torsion-free index-2 subgroups giving elliptic coverings, and using cuspidal quotient factorisations; ensures group-theoretic identification of decomposition groups of removed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belyi cuspidalisation reconstructability (Theorem 3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is an orbicurve over sub-p-adic k of strictly Belyi type, then from the profinite groups (π1)X and its geometric kernel one can group-theoretically reconstruct the set of surjections π1(UX) → π1(X) for open subschemes UX defined over number fields, and the decomposition groups at points in X \ UX for such UX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions: X strictly Belyi type, sub-p-adic base field, use of (GC), cuspidal quotients and tripod (genus 0 with three cusps) reductions. The procedure reconstructs surjections corresponding to open subschemes defined over number fields (one does not have to specify the open immersion explicitly), then recovers decomposition groups as images of cuspidal decomposition groups via these surjections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction of decomposition groups from π1 for strictly Belyi hyperbolic orbicurves (Corollary 3.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be a hyperbolic orbicurve over a non-Archimedean local field k of strictly Belyi type. Then from the profinite group π1(X) alone one can reconstruct the set of decomposition groups at all closed points of X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from Belyi cuspidalisation and finite approximation lemmas (Lemma 3.10). Useful practical criterion: strict Belyi type + non-Archimedean local base field ⇒ full recovery of decomposition groups from π1(X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterisation of decomposition-group sections (Lemma 3.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For X a hyperbolic curve over a non-Archimedean local field k defined over a number field, and a section s: G_k → π1(X) with Im(s) not contained in any cuspidal decomposition group, the following are equivalent: (1) Im(s) is a decomposition group D_x for some x ∈ X(k); (2) for every j ≥ 1, the finite-level subgroup π1(X)[j; s] contains a decomposition group of an algebraic closed point of X which surjects onto G_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a practical finite-level criterion to detect whether a Galois section comes from a rational point: check its approximations at finite characteristic quotients (π1[j; s]) contain decomposition groups surjecting to G_k. Use compactness/Krasner-type approximation arguments as in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uchida-style reconstruction of additive structure of function field (Proposition 3.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a functorial algorithm for constructing the additive structure on k(X) ∪ {0} from the following data: (a) the abstract multiplicative group k(X)^×, (b) the set of surjective valuation maps V_X := {ord_x : k(X)^× → Z}_x∈X(k), and (c) for each v ∈ V_X the subgroup U_v := {f ∈ k(X)^× | f(x)=1} ⊂ k(X)^×.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm summary (as in the text): reconstruct the constant field k from ⋂ ker(v); recover evaluations on ker(v) using decomposition ker(v)=U_v × k^×; reconstruct divisors and spaces L(D) multiplicatively; using special choices of divisors/points (Lemma 3.11) recover additions of constants and then extend to full addition on k(X)∪{0} by pointwise evaluation on ker(ord_x). This is an explicit, stepwise reconstruction: list of required input data and 6 main steps are given in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic orientation (cyclotome) and cyclotomic rigidity for inertia (Definition 3.13 & Proposition 3.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the cyclotome/orientation bZ(π1(X)) := Hom(H^2(π1^geom(X); bZ), bZ) (with a standard multiplicative correction for genus <2 via covers). Proposition (Cyclotomic Rigidity): for X of genus ≥2 (or via cover) and U = X \\ {x}, the canonical identification arising from spectral sequences gives a group-theoretic reconstruction of the natural isomorphism bZ(π1(X)) ≃ I_x (inertia subgroup ≃ bZ(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this rigidity to identify inertia subgroups with the cyclotomic orientation in a group-theoretic manner; when genus<2, pass to a finite étale covering of genus ≥2 and use functorial normalization factors. This identification is used to recover inertia subgroups from cohomological/cyclotomic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity of the Kummer map under Kummer-faithful hypothesis (Lemma 3.15 (part))
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume k is Kummer-faithful and X is proper. Then the composite map U: O(U)^× → H^1(π1(U); bZ(k(X))) (the Kummer map composed with natural identification) is injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kummer-faithfulness of the base field is a necessary hypothesis to ensure injectivity of Kummer maps used in later reconstructions; check the Kummer-faithful property of k before relying on injectivity for distinguishing functions from cohomology classes.
